```{r setup, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
options(width = 76)
# A figure whose pixels are all opaque is written without its alpha channel:
# the same pixels in a smaller file.
opaque_png <- function(path) {
  x <- png::readPNG(path)
  if (length(dim(x)) == 3 && dim(x)[3] == 4 && all(x[, , 4] == 1)) {
    png::writePNG(x[, , 1:3], path)
  }
  path
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 4.6, out.width = "100%", dpi = 117,
                      fig.process = if (requireNamespace("png", quietly = TRUE)) opaque_png)
```

**arraydesign** designs acoustic receiver arrays and tests how well a tracking system performs,
for a new study or for refining or auditing an array already in the water. It places receivers
on a depth raster, maps the share of the water they hear, walks simulated animals through it,
and scores the positions estimated from their detections against the true tracks. This page
runs it end to end on a 20-receiver array on Stoney Lake, Ontario, the example data
included with the package.

Three articles demonstrate further functionality. [Design an array for your own water
body](design-an-array.html) starts from your own raster, station lists and range test, compares
candidate layouts and writes the stations for the field crew. [Specifying and testing movement
models](movement-models.html) sets the walk for your species, a behaviour switching model
between moving and resting, and a goal-oriented model with start and end points.
[Simulate and score an array step by step](simulate-detections.html) runs each stage of
`evaluate_array()` on its own, as a table you can inspect or change.

## 1. Place receivers on Stoney Lake

The depth raster is Stoney Lake at 100 m resolution, with land as `NA`. Depth is zero or
negative metres; 56 of its 4,818 water cells hold 0. It has the same grid and depths as
`depth_raster` of positionR 1.7.0, with the CRS set to EPSG:32617. `terra::rast()` reads it;
the print gives its extent, resolution and depth range.

```{r read-lake}
# Load the package, and ggplot2 for the maps
library(arraydesign)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the depth raster included with the package
lake <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif",
                                package = "arraydesign"))
lake
```

Receivers go in water at least 1 m deep. `terra::ifel()` sets the shallower cells to `NA`, and
`place_receivers()` lays a regular grid of 20 receivers over the rest. It returns their
projected coordinates, their latitude and longitude for the field crew, and the depth under
each (`deploy_z`). It also places random arrays (`method = "random"`) and stations you have
planned (`method = "manual"`).

```{r place-on-raster}
# Set water shallower than 1 m to NA, so that no receiver goes there
deployable <- terra::ifel(abs(lake) < 1, NA, lake)

# Lay a grid of 20 receivers over the deployable water
receivers <- place_receivers(deployable, n = 20, method = "grid", seed = 1)
head(receivers)

# Print the depth range under the receivers, m
range(receivers$deploy_z)
```

The receivers sit in `r sprintf("%.1f", min(receivers$deploy_z))` to
`r sprintf("%.1f", max(receivers$deploy_z))` m of water. `plot()` draws the layout on its lake.

```{r place-receivers, fig.height = 4.6, fig.alt = "The 20 receivers of the grid on Stoney Lake as yellow rings with their names, over the lake drawn by depth."}
# Map the layout over the lake
plot(receivers, lake)
```

*The 20 receivers of the grid on Stoney Lake.*

## 2. Build the detection field and map coverage

The range model gives the probability that a receiver hears one transmission at a given
distance and receiver depth. The
[**detfield**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/) R package, which builds detection
fields and positions animals, sets it in one of two ways. `detfield::de_model()` wraps a model
you fitted to your own range-test data, and `detfield::de_logistic()` makes a stand-in curve
from two distances for a study with no range test; neither estimates a model from range-test
data for you. The example uses the stand-in and assumes all of its values: no range test
measured them, and the range test included with **detfield** is simulated from them. It takes the distances at which 50% and 5% of transmissions are heard (`d50`, `d05`) to be 250 m and 500 m
for a receiver 1 m deep and 750 m and 1,500 m at 35 m, interpolated between. [Design an array
for your own water body](design-an-array.html#the-range-model-yours-or-the-default) takes a
model fitted to your own range test.

```{r range-model}
# Set the assumed range model: d50 and d05 for receivers 1 m and 35 m deep
range_model <- detfield::de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500),
                                     depth = c(1, 35))
range_model
```

**detfield** measures the distance through water from each receiver to each water cell and
reads the curve there, so a receiver does not hear across a point of land.
`detfield::de_field()` returns the detection field, one probability per receiver and cell.

```{r detection-field-build}
# Measure the distance through water from each receiver to each water cell
distances <- detfield::water_distances(lake, receivers)

# Read the curve at each distance: one probability per receiver and cell
field <- detfield::de_field(distances, range_model)
```

The message from `de_field()` counts the receiver and cell pairs with `p >= 0.05` that have land
on the straight line between them. A curve from `de_logistic()` reads a pair with land on the
line at the distance through water; `blocked` in `?detfield::de_model` sets how much less
such pairs hear.

`coverage_summary()` counts, at each threshold, the cells that at least one receiver hears on its
own (`n_cells`).

```{r coverage-summary}
# Count the cells one receiver alone hears at p >= 0.5 and p >= 0.8
coverage_summary(field)
```

The array as a whole hears a cell when any receiver hears the transmission, which takes in cells
between receivers that no single one reaches. The chance that one or more receivers hear it is
one minus the product of the misses (Pedersen et al. 2014, *Methods in Ecology and Evolution*
5: 1043-1051, DOI 10.1111/2041-210X.12255).

```{r array-probability}
# Compute the chance that one or more receivers hear, per water cell
array_p <- data.frame(p = 1 - apply(1 - field$p, 1, prod),
                      terra::xyFromCell(lake, field$cells))

# Count the cells at p >= 0.5 under the array, and all water cells
c(cells_at_0.5 = sum(array_p$p >= 0.5), water_cells = nrow(array_p))
```

The array hears `r format(sum(array_p$p >= 0.5), big.mark = ",")` cells
(`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(array_p$p >= 0.5))` of the water) at 0.5 or more, against
`r coverage_summary(field)$n_cells[1]` under one receiver alone. Most of the lake lies outside
the 50% range of every receiver, so the array hears animals as they pass.

```{r detection-field, fig.height = 4.2, fig.alt = "Detection probability on Stoney Lake under the 20 receivers: bright patches round each yellow ring, most of the lake dark."}
# Take the ring colours of the positionR maps
ring <- detfield::positionr_ring_colours()

# Map the array's detection probability, with the receivers on top as a dark
# ring under a coloured one; the shape scale keys them
ggplot(array_p, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_raster(aes(fill = p)) +
  detfield::scale_fill_probability(name = "Detection\nprobability") +
  geom_point(data = receivers, aes(shape = "Receiver"), colour = ring[["edge"]],
             size = 1.3, stroke = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = receivers, aes(shape = "Receiver"), colour = ring[["heard"]],
             size = 1.3, stroke = 0.45) +
  scale_shape_manual(name = NULL, values = c(Receiver = 21)) +
  coord_equal(expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Easting (m)", y = "Northing (m)") +
  detfield::annotation_scale_bar(location = "br") +
  detfield::theme_positionr()
```

*Probability that at least one of the 20 receivers hears one transmission from
each of the `r format(nrow(array_p), big.mark = ",")` water cells of Stoney Lake, 100 m on a
side.*

## 3. Set a movement model

`crw_model()` builds a correlated random walk from a mean and standard deviation of step length
per time step and a standard deviation of the turning angle. The walk here moves 30 m a minute
with turns of standard deviation 40 degrees; no species was measured to set these values.
[Specifying and testing movement models](movement-models.html) sets a walk for your species, a
switch between moving and resting, release points and a goal.

```{r movement-walk}
# Build a correlated random walk: gamma steps, wrapped normal turns,
# 60 s a step
walk <- crw_model(step_mean = 30, step_sd = 15, turn_sd = 40, time_step_s = 60)
walk
```

## 4. Simulate animals and their detections

`evaluate_array()` walks the animals from random water cells, sends their tags' transmissions
at a random delay of 120 to 180 s, gives each receiver one chance to hear each transmission at
the probability of the field, and
positions the animals from what was heard. This is the reference run of the
[**arraydesignR**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/arraydesignR/) R package, the
point-and-click application of **arraydesign**: 20 animals for 6 hours.
[Simulate and score an array step by step](simulate-detections.html) runs each of these stages
on its own. The delay is a setting, the `tag_delay` element of `control`: its default is 65 to
185 s, a tag programmed at 60 to 180 s with a 5 s transmission, and this page sets it to 120 to
180 s. Give the delay of your own tags, one number or the shortest and longest, in seconds.

```{r evaluate}
# Simulate 20 animals for 6 hours, detect, position and score them
evaluation <- evaluate_array(receivers, lake, range_model, n_animals = 20,
                             seed = 1,
                             control = list(hours = 6, tag_delay = c(120, 180),
                                            movement = walk))
evaluation
```

The detection rate of an animal is the share of its transmissions heard by at least one
receiver.

```{r detection-rate}
# Take the transmissions, with the number of receivers that heard each
sent <- evaluation$detections$transmissions

# Compute the share of each animal's transmissions heard by any receiver
rate_per_animal <- tapply(sent$n_detections > 0, sent$path_id, mean)
c(mean = mean(rate_per_animal), median = median(rate_per_animal),
  never_heard = sum(rate_per_animal == 0))
```

`r sum(sent$n_detections > 0)` transmissions were heard. The mean detection rate per animal is
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(rate_per_animal))`, and `r sum(rate_per_animal == 0)` of the 20
animals were never heard. Counting the detections of each receiver separates the receivers
that heard the animals from those that heard none.

```{r receiver-detections}
# Count the detections of each receiver; a receiver that heard none counts 0
heard_at <- evaluation$detections$detections$receiver_serial
receiver_counts <- data.frame(
  station_id = receivers$station_id, x = receivers$x, y = receivers$y,
  detections = as.vector(table(factor(heard_at,
                                      levels = receivers$receiver_serial)))
)

# List the stations that heard none of the animals
receiver_counts$station_id[receiver_counts$detections == 0]
```

The receivers that heard none lie in the middle of the lake, where no track came within range
in the six hours; the heard transmissions cluster round the rest.

```{r simulate-animals, fig.height = 4.6, fig.alt = "Pale grey tracks of 20 animals on Stoney Lake from white start points, green points where a transmission was heard and small red crosses where it was not, with yellow rings sized by detections and white rings for the receivers that heard nothing."}
# Take the water cells, with depth as positive metres
water <- terra::as.data.frame(abs(lake), xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
names(water)[3] <- "depth_m"

# Take the first position of each track, its start
tracks_table <- as.data.frame(evaluation$tracks)
starts <- tracks_table[!duplicated(tracks_table$path_id), ]

# Map the water, the tracks, the misses, the heard transmissions, the starts
# and the receivers, in that order; the colour scale keys the marks
ggplot(tracks_table, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_raster(data = water, aes(fill = depth_m)) +
  detfield::scale_fill_depth() +
  geom_path(aes(group = path_id, colour = "Track"), linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(data = sent[sent$n_detections == 0, ], aes(colour = "Not heard"),
             shape = 4, size = 0.35, stroke = 0.25, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(data = sent[sent$n_detections > 0, ], aes(colour = "Heard"),
             shape = 21, fill = "#2ECC40", size = 1.7, stroke = 0.3) +
  geom_point(data = starts, aes(colour = "Start"), shape = 21, fill = "white",
             size = 1.8, stroke = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = NULL, breaks = c("Track", "Start", "Heard", "Not heard"),
    values = c(Track = "grey85", Start = "black", Heard = "black",
               `Not heard` = "red3"),
    # The key draws the cross larger than the map does, so that it reads
    guide = guide_legend(position = "bottom",
                         override.aes = list(size = c(1, 1.8, 1.7, 1.6),
                                             stroke = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.3, 0.6),
                                             alpha = 1))
  ) +
  detfield::layer_receivers(receiver_counts, count = "detections",
                            size = 3.4) +
  coord_equal(expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Easting (m)", y = "Northing (m)") +
  detfield::annotation_scale_bar(location = "br") +
  detfield::theme_positionr()
```

*Tracks of the 20 simulated animals over 6 hours, from their starts, and their
`r format(nrow(sent), big.mark = ",")` transmissions, heard by at least one receiver or not.
Of the 20 receivers, `r sum(receiver_counts$detections > 0)`
heard at least one transmission and `r sum(receiver_counts$detections == 0)` heard none.*

## 5. Score positions

For each animal-hour with a detection, `evaluate_array()` counts the detections per receiver
with `detfield::bin_detections()`, computes a location surface with
`detfield::location_surface()`, and measures the distance from the surface's mean to the
animal's mean true position in the hour. The location surface is the positioning method of
**detfield**: for one animal and one hour, the likelihood of each listening receiver's count of
detections over the water cells, under a flat prior and normalised to sum to one; by default the
binomial likelihood, which uses the detections and the misses (`?detfield::location_surface`;
[the model](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/articles/positioning.html)). A study may position its
animals by another method from the same detection set; the
[**detqc**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detqc/) R package writes it in the forms the glatos
and actel R packages and the trackyverse ATO read (`detqc::to_glatos()`, `detqc::to_actel()` and
`detqc::to_ato()`). The hit rate is the mean,
over animal-hours, of the share of the hour's true positions that fall inside the surface's 95%
region.

Only an animal-hour with a detection can be positioned with a location surface, here a share of
`r sprintf("%.3f", evaluation$score$overall$scored_share)` of the
`r evaluation$score$overall$n_animal_hours` animal-hours, and the median error of those scored
is `r round(evaluation$score$overall$median_error_mean_m)` m. The hit rate,
`r sprintf("%.3f", evaluation$score$overall$hit_rate)`, is below 0.95 because a surface assumes
the animal stayed in one place for the hour, and these animals swim about
`r sprintf("%.1f", 30 * 60 / 1000)` km in an hour. `plot()` maps the error of each scored
animal-hour.

```{r evaluate-array, fig.height = 4.6, fig.alt = "Points at the true positions of the scored animal-hours on Stoney Lake, coloured by positioning error in four classes, with yellow rings for the receivers that heard the animals and white rings for those that heard none."}
# Map the positioning error of each scored animal-hour
plot(evaluation)
```

*Positioning error of each of the `r evaluation$score$overall$n_bins` scored animal-hours: the
distance from the mean of the hourly location surface to the animal's mean true position in the
hour, drawn at that position.*
